To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of survivin in breast tumors is a strong independent predictor of poor clinical outcome, that survivin expression is significantly associated with the expression of HER2, VGF, urokinases and PAI- 1, that the association between HER2 expression and survivin expression is not mediated by the other factors, and that the association between urokinase expression and survivin is mediated by PAI-1 expression.
survivin is a novel prognostic marker for breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of Survivin in breast cancer and its association with clinical parameters, and with the expression of HER2, uPA, PAI-1, VEGF and p53 in breast cancer.
a novel approach to the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of cancer.
the development of a mathematical model for the prediction of breast cancer survival based on the expression of survivin in tumor cells and other factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study suggest that the expression of survivin in breast cancer may predict clinical outcome and is related to HER-2, VEGFA, uPA and PAI- 1.
the expression of Survivin is associated with a poor prognosis in breast cancer.
the expression of survivin is a prognostic marker of survival in patients with invasive breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
survivin is a novel and promising target for the treatment of breast cancer.
we have demonstrated the utility of a novel approach to identify and characterize the molecular determinants of the metastatic cascade in breast cancer.
survivin expression is an independent prognostic factor for breast cancer patients, especially in those who have HER2-positive tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown the importance of survivin in breast cancer.
we have developed a new method for the detection and quantification of circulating tumor cells (CTC) from the blood of breast cancer patients.
